purpose.statement: Provide a deterministic, provider-neutral orchestration runtime that turns approved goals into accepted software through explicit modular engineering contracts, evidence, gates, and traceable lifecycle progression.

businessObjectives.statement: Make software-engineering progression reproducible and fail closed when required inputs, evidence, or approvals are invalid.
Allow best-in-class engineering capabilities to be replaced without changing canonical workflow semantics or generic Core.
Require scoped verification and evidence before work, changes, systems, or business outcomes advance.
Trace every approved business objective through requirements, design, planned work, implementation, verification, integration, and acceptance.
Prevent invalid, cyclic, incomplete, or impossible dependency plans from reaching assignment and execution.
Replace dependency-analysis capabilities without changing canonical semantics or generic Core.
Provide authoritative ordering sufficient for downstream systems to identify safely runnable work.

users.name: Engineering workflow author
users.description: A maintainer or engineering lead who configures and operates DevRelay from a goal through business acceptance.
needs: Inspect exact artifacts, decisions, evidence, and progression state.
Run a complete engineering lifecycle without relying on model memory.
Swap compatible adapters without redesigning the workflow.

users.name: Dependency-planning workflow author
users.description: A maintainer or host operator who runs and reviews dependency analysis before assignment.
needs: Approve only a valid and reviewed DAG.

keyCapabilities.name: Replaceable engineering capabilities
keyCapabilities.description: Bind interchangeable bounded adapters to stable provider-neutral module operations.

keyCapabilities.name: Deterministic lifecycle orchestration
keyCapabilities.description: Route exact state through the approved V1 lifecycle and stop invalid work before it propagates.

keyCapabilities.name: Structured engineering contracts
keyCapabilities.description: Represent requirements, architecture, contracts, work, changes, evidence, and acceptance as versioned artifacts.

keyCapabilities.name: Evidence-based verification and acceptance
keyCapabilities.description: Require scoped evidence at work-item, integrated-system, and business-acceptance boundaries.

keyCapabilities.name: Work dependency analysis
keyCapabilities.description: Analyze an approved work breakdown and propose directed dependencies and dispositions.

keyCapabilities.name: Dependency Gate verification
keyCapabilities.description: Validate graph mechanics and semantic policy before authoritative promotion.

successMetrics.name: Deterministic progression
successMetrics.measure: Repeated Core-owned routing, validation, replay, and gate decisions for identical content-addressed inputs.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run positive, negative, drift, checkpoint, replay, and gate conformance suites.

successMetrics.name: Adapter-independent semantics
successMetrics.measure: Compatible adapter replacements requiring a product-specific behavioral branch in generic Core.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Execute adapter replacement fixtures and scan generic Core for product identifiers.

successMetrics.name: Verified progression
successMetrics.measure: Lifecycle transitions occurring without the configured passing evidence and approval record.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Audit module execution records, gate decisions, verification evidence, and acceptance receipts.

successMetrics.name: Lifecycle trace coverage
successMetrics.measure: Approved business objectives with a complete trace to implementation and passing verification evidence by BusinessAcceptance.
successMetrics.target: 100 percent or an explicit approved disposition.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run TraceabilityGraph coverage and orphan diagnostics at each lifecycle horizon.

successMetrics.name: Generic Core product branches
successMetrics.measure: WorkDependencyAnalysis, Spec Kit, or OpenSpec identifier branches in generic Core.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run static special-case scans and adapter-replacement conformance tests.

successMetrics.name: Unsafe runnable frontier
successMetrics.measure: Work items exposed as runnable while an authoritative predecessor remains incomplete.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Derive runnable frontiers from approved DAG fixtures and predecessor completion state.

successMetrics.name: Invalid dependency progression
successMetrics.measure: Invalid endpoint, duplicate or self edge, cycle, unresolved missing dependency, or impossible ordering cases reaching an approved baseline.
successMetrics.measurementMethod: Run positive and negative WorkDependency Gate fixtures and inspect exact promotion receipts.

scope.statement: RequirementsGathering [module]: RequirementsGathering converts an explicit goal and project context into a canonical requirements candidate and deterministic ProjectOverview candidate.
RequirementsGate [gate]: RequirementsGate validates and approves one exact RequirementsBaseline and ProjectOverviewBaseline pair before architecture progression.
ArchitectureDiscovery [module; conditional]: ArchitectureDiscovery conditionally establishes a validated current-architecture snapshot for an existing repository that has no architecture baseline.
ArchitectureDesign [module]: ArchitectureDesign converts approved requirements into a new architecture candidate or a proposed architecture change.
ArchitectureGate [gate]: ArchitectureGate validates architectural fitness, evidence, and approval before establishing or updating the ArchitectureBaseline.

ContractGeneration [module; conditional]: ContractGeneration conditionally produces and validates API, schema, event, protocol, and other machine-readable interface contracts when the approved design requires them.
WorkBreakdown [module]: WorkBreakdown converts approved scope into a complete set of bounded, traceable, independently executable and verifiable work items without executing them.
WorkDependencyAnalysis [module]: WorkDependencyAnalysis validates authoritative ordering and dependencies between approved work items before assignment or execution.
SpecialistAssignment [module]: SpecialistAssignment selects a compatible human or implementation engine for each ready work item from explicit capability requirements and policy.
WorkExecution [module]: WorkExecution performs one authorized work item against exact inputs and returns bounded deliverables, changes, diagnostics, and evidence without owning acceptance.
WorkItemVerification [module]: WorkItemVerification checks each executed work item against its verification plan and required evidence before it can enter integration.
ChangeIntegration [module]: ChangeIntegration combines individually verified changes in dependency-safe order and records the exact integrated state.
SystemVerification [module]: SystemVerification validates the integrated system across functional, security, performance, operational, documentation, and other configured quality policies.
BusinessAcceptance [module]: BusinessAcceptance evaluates the verified system against approved business objectives, success metrics, scope, and acceptance criteria and records the final disposition.
Bounded replaceable analysis manifests and conformance fixtures.
Provider-neutral dependency analysis bound to exact WorkBreakdown and upstream context.
Dependency state, policy, hint-disposition, edge, finding, candidate, baseline, clarification, diagnostic, and Gate evidence artifacts.
Version-pinned relevant context slicing and pre-proposer coherence validation.
A separate Gate for graph mechanics, semantic policy, approval, and exact promotion.
Pinned OPA policy bundle evaluation and normalized decision evidence.
A bounded post-proposal consistency-review slot with Spec Kit as the V1 binding.
A trusted contributor and candidate-to-approved authority transition.

nonGoals.statement: Build another monolithic coding agent or AI-provider wrapper.
nonGoals.rationale: DevRelay standardizes deterministic engineering workflow rather than code generation.

nonGoals.statement: Treat model confidence, adapter output, chat history, or successful execution as implicit approval.
nonGoals.rationale: Only explicit validated gates and evidence authorize progression.

nonGoals.statement: Reimplement full upstream tools such as OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Structurizr, or MADR inside Core.
nonGoals.rationale: DevRelay invokes only bounded replaceable capabilities.

nonGoals.statement: Add lifecycle modules outside the approved V1 inventory without a new requirements change and overview baseline.
nonGoals.rationale: V1 scope must remain deliberate and auditable.

nonGoals.statement: Choose a specialist, model, agent, or human.
Introduce a distributed scheduler, agent framework, provider wrapper, or general control plane.
nonGoals.rationale: This release is an incremental module slice.

nonGoals.statement: Execute, implement, test, or verify a work item.
Persist schedules, estimates, capacity, or runtime execution waves.
nonGoals.rationale: Scheduling depends on changing runtime state.

constraints.statement: Every stage must exchange canonical structured artifacts and cannot rely on conversational memory as authority.
constraints.rationale: Explicit artifacts make lifecycle state reproducible and verifiable.

constraints.statement: Producing modules cannot approve or promote their own candidates; configured gates own progression decisions.
constraints.rationale: Separate authority prevents production from becoming self-approval.

constraints.statement: V1 lifecycle scope is limited to the fourteen owner-approved components recorded in the project overview.
constraints.rationale: A closed inventory prevents silent V1 scope expansion.

constraints.statement: Canonical Core and module contracts cannot depend on one AI model, provider, IDE, or external engineering product.
constraints.rationale: The workflow owns engineering semantics; tools only perform bounded capabilities.

constraints.statement: WorkDependencyAnalysis is analysis and approval, not assignment, scheduling, or execution.
constraints.rationale: Separate lifecycle authority prevents planned ordering from becoming an execution claim.

constraints.statement: Canonical contracts and Core cannot depend on a model, Spec Kit, OpenSpec, or another analyzer product.
Traceability stores forward dependency assertions only and derives reverse traversal at query time.
constraints.rationale: One direction avoids duplicated inconsistent facts.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Core-owned routing, validation, checkpoint replay, traceability projection, and gate preparation must be deterministic for exact inputs.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Canonical route, result, diagnostic, update, and receipt digest equality.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100 percent equality for deterministic Core-owned behavior.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Canonical lifecycle contracts must remain independent of IDE, AI provider, model, operating host, and bounded external tool.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Compatible host and adapter substitutions requiring canonical contract changes.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Every accepted lifecycle assertion must retain exact artifact, contributor, execution, authority, and graph-version provenance.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Accepted graph assertions lacking complete resolvable provenance.

nonFunctionalRequirements.statement: Routing, mechanical validation, canonical ordering, replay, and Gate commit preparation must be deterministic for exact inputs.
nonFunctionalRequirements.measure: Canonical output, diagnostic, route, and replay digest equality.
nonFunctionalRequirements.target: 100 percent equality for deterministic Core-owned behavior.

terminology.definition: A lifecycle module invoked only when exact Core-owned state and approved policy satisfy its declared condition.
A separate validation and approval boundary that decides whether an exact candidate may become an approved baseline or progress downstream.
A provider-neutral lifecycle contract defining exact inputs, action, outputs, outcomes, evidence, and progression boundary.
The compact approved project-wide context deterministically projected from the paired RequirementsBaseline and explicitly supplied to downstream modules.
A Core-owned cross-cutting lifecycle index that records validated artifact relationships beside the module sequence without becoming a workflow stage.
The complete immutable projection of one exact approved WorkBreakdownBaseline used as the work-item universe for a single full dependency analysis.
A deterministic, relevance-declared extraction from one immutable version-pinned source artifact, supplied as explicit analyzer input with its own content digest.
A directed acyclic graph where each forward edge says one predecessor must complete before one successor may start.
The evidence-backed treatment of one non-authoritative WorkBreakdown dependency hint.
A dependency forbidden by exact domain, architecture, contract, repository, or policy evidence even when acyclic.
Work items whose authoritative predecessors are complete under current runtime state.
